ai.title: Update README branding, fix typos, add test-diff script
ai.summary: npm-app/README.md updated: title changed to 'The AI tool for senior engineers', description rewritten, typo fixed ('paried'->'paired'), undo/redo instructions changed from `Ctrl+U`/`Ctrl+R` to `undo`/`redo` commands. test/package.json adds 'test-diff' script running generate-patch.test.ts.

eli5.text: The product has updated its marketing banner and project description, fixing a spelling error and simplifying the undo/redo instructions in its user guide. If you opened the project's main documentation today, you'd see the heading now reads 'The AI tool for senior engineers' instead of the previous product name, and the tips section now tells you to type 'undo' or 'redo' rather than using keyboard shortcuts. These are visible changes to documentation only; the assistant's behavior is unchanged.

ai.title: Remove automatic git staging from CLI
ai.summary: Removed the `stageChanges` helper and its call from `npm-app/src/cli.ts`, along with the now-unused `child_process.exec` import. The helper previously ran `git add .` in the project root immediately before sending user input, and the change stops that automatic staging behavior. Scope is the CLI only; chat messages are still stored and processed, but the working tree is no longer staged as a side effect.

eli5.text: When you interact with the command-line version of the assistant, it will no longer automatically save or prepare your project files for the next step without asking you first. Previously, the tool would run a background command to gather and stage all your changes right before sending your input, but this happened silently and without your control. Now, that automatic prep step has been removed, so your files aren't touched until you explicitly decide to save or commit them. This affects only people using the command-line interface.

ai.title: Increase OpenAI timeout to 120s
ai.summary: OpenAI request timeouts doubled from 60s to 120s in `promptOpenAI` and `promptOpenAIWithContinuation` within `backend/src/openai-api.ts`. This accommodates longer-running completions and streaming responses without premature aborts.

eli5.text: The system now waits up to two minutes, instead of one, for the AI assistant to finish generating a response before giving up. This helps when the assistant needs more time to answer longer or more complex questions, so replies are less likely to cut off midway. If you use the assistant and your question takes a bit longer to process, it should now complete instead of timing out. This change is live today.

ai.title: Project file context cache keyed by cwd
ai.summary: getProjectFileContext now derives contextRoot from current working directory relative to project root. Cache invalidation triggers when currentWorkingDirectory mismatches contextRoot, preventing stale file trees after directory changes. Affects npm-app/src/project-files.ts. README trimmed.

eli5.text: When you open a new folder inside your project, the assistant no longer shows you the file list from the project's main folder, it refreshes to show files in the folder you're actually looking at. Previously, switching directories kept the old file tree around, which could leave you editing the wrong place. Now the assistant notices when your view changes and updates its mental map accordingly.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.52
ai.summary: Incremented package version from 1.0.51 to 1.0.52 in backend and npm-app manifests. Applies to backend/package.json and npm-app/package.json. Routine release preparation.

eli5.text: The software was quietly restarted with a new version number, 1.0.52, replacing the previous 1.0.51 in both its main brain and its app launcher, as a routine step before its next public release. You, as a user, won't notice anything different right away because this change just updates a label, it's like renumbering a product box on a shelf. The change is live today in the code, but it's just housekeeping: no features, fixes, or speed changes are included here, just the version bump itself.
